editorial.description_en: The ink at the bottom of the stone, where it has thickened. The darkest colour in the corpus, and still not black.
editorial.description_ja: 硯の底にたまった墨のような、いちばん濃い色。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: Deliberately not black. A true black gives a garment palette nothing to sit against, and it is also the one value a camera estimate is least able to distinguish.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.186, C 0.005, h 268.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 底 (soko, bottom) + 墨 (sumi, ink), rendaku to -zumi. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Deep Ink" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 底墨. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — yoru-gami at ΔE00 6.6, shimo-yo at ΔE00 8.8, kuro-tsuchi at ΔE00 10.2. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.005 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
